sanskrit: nidāghakāle varṣe vā yaś chatraṃ saṃprayacchati nāsya kaś cin manodāhaḥ kadā cid api jāyate kṛcchrāt sa viṣamāc caiva vipra mokṣam avāpnute
english: Whoever bestows an umbrella in the hot season or in the rains, no anguish of mind ever arises in him; and from hardship and from peril, O brāhmaṇa, he wins deliverance.

sanskrit: pradānaṃ sarvadānānāṃ śakaṭasya viśiṣyate evam āha mahābhāgaḥ śāṇḍilyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: Of all gifts, the gift of a cart is the most excellent—thus declared the greatly blessed and venerable seer Śāṇḍilya.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dahyamānāya viprāya yaḥ prayacchaty upānahau yat phalaṃ tasya bhavati tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a man gives a pair of sandals to a brāhmaṇa whose feet are scorched, what fruit accrues to him—tell me that, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca upānahau prayacched yo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samāhitaḥ mardate kaṇṭakān sarvān viṣamān nistaraty api sa śatrūṇām upari ca saṃtiṣṭhati yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: He who, with collected mind, bestows a pair of sandals upon brāhmaṇas tramples down all thorns and crosses over every rough place; and he stands triumphant above his foes, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yānaṃ cāśvatarīyuktaṃ tasya śubhraṃ viśāṃ pate upatiṣṭhati kaunteya rūpyakāñcanabhūṣaṇam śakaṭaṃ damyasaṃyuktaṃ dattaṃ bhavati caiva hi
english: A gleaming carriage yoked with she-mules, adorned with silver and gold, attends upon him, O lord of peoples, O son of Kuntī; and it is as though he had given a cart yoked with trained oxen.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yat phalaṃ tiladāne ca bhūmidāne ca kīrtitam gopradāne 'nnadāne ca bhūyas tad brūhi kaurava
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The fruit that is proclaimed in the gift of sesame and the gift of land, in the gift of a cow and the gift of food—tell me of that once more, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇuṣva mama kaunteya tiladānasya yat phalam niśamya ca yathānyāyaṃ prayaccha kurusattama
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear from me, O son of Kuntī, what fruit the gift of sesame yields; and having heard it, bestow it duly, O best of the Kurus.

sanskrit: pitṝṇāṃ prathamaṃ bhojyaṃ tilāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayaṃbhuvā tiladānena vai tasmāt pitṛpakṣaḥ pramodate
english: Sesame seeds were created by the Self-Existent as the foremost food of the ancestors; therefore by the gift of sesame the company of the fathers rejoices.

sanskrit: māghamāse tilān yas tu brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati sarvasattvasamākīrṇaṃ narakaṃ sa na paśyati
english: He who in the month of Māgha gives sesame to brāhmaṇas does not behold the hell thronged with every kind of creature.

sanskrit: sarvakāmaiḥ sa yajate yas tilair yajate pitṝn na cākāmena dātavyaṃ tilaśrāddhaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: He who honors the ancestors with sesame worships them with all desired things fulfilled; yet the sesame śrāddha must never be offered grudgingly, against one's will.

sanskrit: maharṣeḥ kaśyapasyaite gātrebhyaḥ prasṛtās tilāḥ tato divyaṃ gatā bhāvaṃ pradāneṣu tilāḥ prabho
english: These sesame seeds sprang forth from the limbs of the great seer Kaśyapa; thence, O lord, sesame attained a divine nature among the offerings of gifts.

sanskrit: pauṣṭikā rūpadāś caiva tathā pāpavināśanāḥ tasmāt sarvapradānebhyas tiladānaṃ viśiṣyate
english: They give nourishment, they bestow beauty, and they are destroyers of sin; therefore, of all gifts, the gift of sesame is the most excellent.

sanskrit: āpastambaś ca medhāvī śaṅkhaś ca likhitas tathā maharṣir gautamaś cāpi tiladānair divaṃ gatāḥ
english: The sagacious Āpastamba, and Śaṅkha, and Likhita, and the great seer Gautama too—all went to heaven by gifts of sesame.

sanskrit: tilahomaparā viprāḥ sarve saṃyatamaithunāḥ samā gavyena haviṣā pravṛttiṣu ca saṃsthitāḥ
english: Brāhmaṇas devoted to the sesame oblation, all restrained in their pleasures, are reckoned the equals of those who offer the oblation of cow's products and who abide steadfast in their observances.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ tiladānaṃ paraṃ smṛtam akṣayaṃ sarvadānānāṃ tiladānam ihocyate
english: Of all gifts whatsoever, the gift of sesame is held to be supreme; among all gifts, the gift of sesame is here declared imperishable.

sanskrit: utpanne ca purā havye kuśikarṣiḥ paraṃtapa tilair agnitrayaṃ hutvā prāptavān gatim uttamām
english: And of old, when the oblation had been produced, the seer Kuśika, O scorcher of foes, having offered into the three fires with sesame, attained the highest goal.

sanskrit: iti proktaṃ kuruśreṣṭha tiladānam anuttamam vidhānaṃ yena vidhinā tilānām iha śasyate
english: Thus has the unsurpassed gift of sesame been declared, O foremost of the Kurus, together with the rite by which the offering of sesame is here commended.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ nibodhedaṃ devānāṃ yaṣṭum icchatām samāgamaṃ mahārāja brahmaṇā vai svayaṃbhuvā
english: Hereafter learn of this, O great king—how the gods, desiring to perform a sacrifice, came together with the Self-Existent Brahmā.

sanskrit: devāḥ sametya brahmāṇaṃ bhūmibhāgaṃ yiyakṣavaḥ śubhaṃ deśam ayācanta yajema iti pārthiva
english: The gods, having assembled before Brahmā and wishing to sacrifice, begged for a portion of earth, an auspicious tract: "Let us perform the sacrifice," O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ bhagavaṃs tvaṃ prabhur bhūmeḥ sarvasya tridivasya ca yajemahi mahābhāga yajñaṃ bhavadanujñayā nānanujñātabhūmir hi yajñasya phalam aśnute
english: The gods said: O Blessed One, you are the lord of all the earth and of the threefold heaven; with your leave, O greatly blessed one, let us perform the sacrifice, for on unsanctioned ground no one wins the fruit of a sacrifice.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi sarvasya jagataḥ sthāvarasya carasya ca prabhur bhavasi tasmāt tvaṃ samanujñātum arhasi
english: For you are the lord of the whole world, both the moving and the unmoving; therefore it is fitting that you grant us your sanction.

sanskrit: brahmovāca dadāmi medinībhāgaṃ bhavadbhyo 'haṃ surarṣabhāḥ yasmin deśe kariṣyadhvaṃ yajñaṃ kāśyapanandanāḥ
english: Brahmā said: I give you a portion of the earth, O bulls among the gods, the tract whereon you shall perform your sacrifice, O sons of Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ bhagavan kṛtakāmāḥ smo yakṣyāmas tv āptadakṣiṇaiḥ imaṃ tu deśaṃ munayaḥ paryupāsanta nityadā
english: The gods said: O Blessed One, our wish is fulfilled; we shall sacrifice with the prescribed fees duly rendered—and this very tract the sages have ever frequented and revered.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato 'gastyaś ca kaṇvaś ca bhṛgur atrir vṛṣākapiḥ asito devalaś caiva devayajñam upāgaman
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Agastya and Kaṇva, Bhṛgu, Atri, Vṛṣākapi, and Asita Devala came to the gods' sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato devā mahātmāna ījire yajñam acyuta tathā samāpayām āsur yathākālaṃ surarṣabhāḥ
english: Then the high-souled gods performed the sacrifice, O unfailing one, and the bulls among the gods brought it to its completion in due season.

sanskrit: ta iṣṭayajñās tridaśā himavaty acalottame ṣaṣṭham aṃśaṃ kratos tasya bhūmidānaṃ pracakrire
english: Having performed their sacrifice, the thirty gods upon Himavat, that loftiest of mountains, made the gift of land a sixth part of that rite.

sanskrit: prādeśamātraṃ bhūmes tu yo dadyād anupaskṛtam na sīdati sa kṛcchreṣu na ca durgāṇy avāpnute
english: Whoever gives even a span's measure of land, unencumbered, does not sink in times of hardship nor fall into straits.

sanskrit: śītavātātapasahāṃ gṛhabhūmiṃ susaṃskṛtām pradāya suralokasthaḥ puṇyānte 'pi na cālyate
english: Having given a well-prepared plot for a dwelling, proof against cold, wind, and heat, a man dwells in the world of the gods and is not dislodged even when his merit is spent.

sanskrit: mudito vasate prājñaḥ śakreṇa saha pārthiva pratiśrayapradātā ca so 'pi svarge mahīyate
english: The wise man dwells in joy together with Śakra, O son of Pṛthā; and the giver of shelter, he too is exalted in heaven.

sanskrit: adhyāpakakule jātaḥ śrotriyo niyatendriyaḥ gṛhe yasya vaset tuṣṭaḥ pradhānaṃ lokam aśnute
english: He in whose house a man born in a line of teachers, learned in the Vedas and of subdued senses, dwells contented—that giver attains the foremost world.

sanskrit: tathā gavārthe śaraṇaṃ śītavarṣasahaṃ mahat āsaptamaṃ tārayati kulaṃ bharatasattama
english: Likewise, a great shelter for the sake of cattle, proof against cold and rain, redeems one's line down to the seventh generation, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kṣetrabhūmiṃ dadal loke putra śriyam avāpnuyāt ratnabhūmiṃ pradattvā tu kulavaṃśaṃ vivardhayet
english: By giving farmland in this world, my son, a man would gain prosperity; and by bestowing a tract rich in gems, he would cause his family line to flourish.

sanskrit: na coṣarāṃ na nirdagdhāṃ mahīṃ dadyāt kathaṃ cana na śmaśānaparītāṃ ca na ca pāpaniṣevitām
english: But one should never give land that is barren and salt, nor land scorched and burnt, nor land bordered by a cremation ground, nor land used for wicked deeds.

sanskrit: pārakye bhūmideśe tu pitṝṇāṃ nirvapet tu yaḥ tad bhūmisvāmipitṛbhiḥ śrāddhakarma vihanyate
english: When a man makes an offering to the ancestors upon a tract of land belonging to another, that funerary rite is despoiled by the fathers of the land's owner.

sanskrit: tasmāt krītvā mahīṃ dadyāt svalpām api vicakṣaṇaḥ piṇḍaḥ pitṛbhyo datto vai tasyāṃ bhavati śāśvataḥ
english: Therefore let the discerning man first buy the land, even a little, and then give it; for the rice-ball offered to the fathers upon such ground becomes everlasting.

sanskrit: aṭavīparvatāś caiva nadītīrthāni yāni ca sarvāṇy asvāmikāny āhur na hi tatra parigrahaḥ
english: Forests and mountains, and whatever river-fords there be—all these, they say, are ownerless, for there is no private possession of them.

sanskrit: ity etad bhūmidānasya phalam uktaṃ viśāṃ pate ataḥ paraṃ tu godānaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi te 'nagha
english: Thus has the fruit of the gift of land been told, O lord of peoples; and now, after this, I shall proclaim to you the gift of a cow, O sinless one.

sanskrit: gāvo 'dhikās tapasvibhyo yasmāt sarvebhya eva ca tasmān maheśvaro devas tapas tābhiḥ samāsthitaḥ
english: Since cows are higher than all ascetics whatsoever, therefore the god Maheśvara undertook his austerity in their company.

sanskrit: brahmaloke vasanty etāḥ somena saha bhārata āsāṃ brahmarṣayaḥ siddhāḥ prārthayanti parāṃ gatim
english: These cows dwell in the world of Brahmā together with Soma, O Bhārata; from their midst the perfected brahman-seers seek the supreme goal.

sanskrit: payasā haviṣā dadhnā śakṛtāpy atha carmaṇā asthibhiś copakurvanti śṛṅgair vālaiś ca bhārata
english: With milk, with the clarified offering, with curd, and even with their dung, with their hide, with their bones, with their horns and their hair do they render service, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nāsāṃ śītātapau syātāṃ sadaitāḥ karma kurvate na varṣaṃ viṣamaṃ vāpi duḥkham āsāṃ bhavaty uta
english: Neither cold nor heat afflicts them; ever do they do their work; neither rain nor rough weather brings them any distress.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiḥ sahitā yānti tasmāt parataraṃ padam ekaṃ gobrāhmaṇaṃ tasmāt pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: United with the brāhmaṇas they go to the highest station; therefore the wise speak of cow and brāhmaṇa as one.

sanskrit: rantidevasya yajñe tāḥ paśutvenopakalpitāḥ tataś carmaṇvatī rājan gocarmabhyaḥ pravartitā
english: At the sacrifice of Rantideva they were appointed as sacrificial victims; thence, O king, the river Carmaṇvatī came to flow from the hides of the cattle.

sanskrit: paśutvāc ca vinirmuktāḥ pradānāyopakalpitāḥ tā imā vipramukhyebhyo yo dadāti mahīpate nistared āpadaṃ kṛcchrāṃ viṣamastho 'pi pārthiva
english: Released thereafter from the state of sacrificial victims, they were ordained for giving away; and whoever gives these to the foremost of brāhmaṇas, O lord of earth, would cross over grievous calamity, even though set in dire straits, O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: gavāṃ sahasradaḥ pretya narakaṃ na prapaśyati sarvatra vijayaṃ cāpi labhate manujādhipa
english: He who gives a thousand cows beholds no hell after death and wins victory everywhere, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: amṛtaṃ vai gavāṃ kṣīram ity āha tridaśādhipaḥ tasmād dadāti yo dhenum amṛtaṃ sa prayacchati
english: "The milk of cows is verily the nectar of immortality," so said the lord of the thirty gods; therefore he who gives a milch-cow gives the nectar itself.

sanskrit: agnīnām avyayaṃ hy etad dhaumyaṃ vedavido viduḥ tasmād dadāti yo dhenuṃ sa haumyaṃ saṃprayacchati
english: The knowers of the Veda know this to be the imperishable oblation-stuff of the fires; therefore he who gives a milch-cow bestows the very means of the offering.

sanskrit: svargo vai mūrtimān eṣa vṛṣabhaṃ yo gavāṃ patim vipre guṇayute dadyāt sa vai svarge mahīyate
english: This bull, the lord of the cows, is heaven in bodily form; whoever gives him to a brāhmaṇa endowed with virtues is himself exalted in heaven.

sanskrit: prāṇā vai prāṇinām ete procyante bharatarṣabha tasmād dadāti yo dhenuṃ prāṇān vai sa prayacchati
english: These are declared to be the very life-breaths of living beings, O bull of the Bhāratas; therefore he who gives a milch-cow gives life-breath itself.

sanskrit: gāvaḥ śaraṇyā bhūtānām iti vedavido viduḥ tasmād dadāti yo dhenuṃ śaraṇaṃ saṃprayacchati
english: "Cows are the refuge of creatures," thus the knowers of the Veda know; therefore he who gives a milch-cow bestows refuge itself.

sanskrit: na vadhārthaṃ pradātavyā na kīnāśe na nāstike gojīvine na dātavyā tathā gauḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: A cow must not be given to be slaughtered, nor to a miser, nor to an unbeliever; nor should a cow be given to one who lives by trafficking in cattle, O bull among men.

sanskrit: dadāti tādṛśānāṃ vai naro gāḥ pāpakarmaṇām akṣayaṃ narakaṃ yātīty evam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: The man who gives cows to such evildoers goes to the imperishable hell—so the wise have declared.

sanskrit: na kṛśāṃ pāpavatsāṃ vā vandhyāṃ rogānvitāṃ tathā na vyaṅgāṃ na pariśrāntāṃ dadyād gāṃ brāhmaṇāya vai
english: One should not give to a brāhmaṇa a cow that is emaciated, or one whose calf has come to harm, or one that is barren or diseased, or one that is maimed or worn out.

sanskrit: daśagosahasradaḥ samyak śakreṇa saha modate akṣayāṃl labhate lokān naraḥ śatasahasradaḥ
english: He who duly gives ten thousand cows rejoices together with Śakra; the man who gives a hundred thousand wins imperishable worlds.

sanskrit: ity etad gopradānaṃ ca tiladānaṃ ca kīrtitam tathā bhūmipradānaṃ ca śṛṇuṣvānne ca bhārata
english: Thus the gift of cattle, the gift of sesame, and the gift of land have been proclaimed; now hear concerning the gift of food, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: annadānaṃ pradhānaṃ hi kaunteya paricakṣate annasya hi pradānena rantidevo divaṃ gataḥ
english: The gift of food they declare to be foremost, O son of Kuntī; for by the gift of food Rantideva went to heaven.

sanskrit: śrāntāya kṣudhitāyānnaṃ yaḥ prayacchati bhūmipa svāyaṃbhuvaṃ mahābhāgaṃ sa paśyati narādhipa
english: He who gives food to one weary and hungry, O lord of earth, beholds the greatly blessed son of the Self-Existent, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: na hiraṇyair na vāsobhir nāśvadānena bhārata prāpnuvanti narāḥ śreyo yathehānnapradāḥ prabho
english: Not by gifts of gold, nor of garments, nor by the gift of horses, O Bhārata, do men win such welfare as the givers of food win here, O lord.

sanskrit: annaṃ vai paramaṃ dravyam annaṃ śrīś ca parā matā annāt prāṇaḥ prabhavati tejo vīryaṃ balaṃ tathā
english: Food is verily the supreme substance, and food is deemed the highest prosperity; from food springs life-breath, and likewise vigor, valor, and strength.

sanskrit: sadbhyo dadāti yaś cānnaṃ sadaikāgramanā naraḥ na sa durgāṇy avāpnotīty evam āha parāśaraḥ
english: The man who gives food to the good, ever single-minded, does not fall into straits—thus declared Parāśara.

sanskrit: arcayitvā yathānyāyaṃ devebhyo 'nnaṃ nivedayet yadanno hi naro rājaṃs tadannās tasya devatāḥ
english: Having duly worshipped, one should present the food to the gods; for whatever food a man eats, O king, that same food belongs to his deities.

sanskrit: kaumudyāṃ śuklapakṣe tu yo 'nnadānaṃ karoty uta sa saṃtarati durgāṇi pretya cānantyam aśnute
english: He who makes a gift of food on the full-moon day of Kārttika, in the bright fortnight, crosses over all straits and, after death, partakes of the infinite.

sanskrit: abhuktvātithaye cānnaṃ prayacched yaḥ samāhitaḥ sa vai brahmavidāṃ lokān prāpnuyād bharatarṣabha
english: He who, with collected mind, gives food to a guest before he himself has eaten, would surely attain the worlds of those who know Brahman, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sukṛcchrām āpadaṃ prāptaś cānnadaḥ puruṣas taret pāpaṃ tarati caiveha duṣkṛtaṃ cāpakarṣati
english: Though fallen into the direst calamity, the giver of food crosses over; he crosses beyond sin even here, and casts off his ill deeds.

sanskrit: ity etad annadānasya tiladānasya caiva ha bhūmidānasya ca phalaṃ godānasya ca kīrtitam
english: Thus has the fruit of the gift of food, and of the gift of sesame, and of the gift of land, and of the gift of cattle been proclaimed.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutaṃ dānaphalaṃ tāta yat tvayā parikīrtitam annaṃ tu te viśeṣeṇa praśastam iha bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I have heard the fruit of giving that you have proclaimed, dear father; but food, in your account, is here especially praised, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pānīyadānaṃ paramaṃ kathaṃ ceha mahāphalam ity etac chrotum icchāmi vistareṇa pitāmaha
english: And how is the gift of water supreme here, and of great fruit? This I wish to hear in full, O grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hanta te vartayiṣyāmi yathāvad bharatarṣabha gadatas tan mamādyeha śṛṇu satyaparākrama pānīyadānāt prabhṛti sarvaṃ vakṣyāmi te 'nagha
english: Bhīṣma said: Come, I shall recount it to you faithfully, O bull of the Bhāratas; hearken now as I tell it, O you whose valor is truth; beginning with the gift of water, I shall declare it all to you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: yad annaṃ yac ca pānīyaṃ saṃpradāyāśnute naraḥ na tasmāt paramaṃ dānaṃ kiṃ cid astīti me matiḥ
english: When a man, having given food and water, then enjoys their fruit—there is, in my judgment, no gift higher than this.

sanskrit: annāt prāṇabhṛtas tāta pravartante hi sarvaśaḥ tasmād annaṃ paraṃ loke sarvadāneṣu kathyate
english: From food, dear son, all that bear life come forth in every way; therefore food is called supreme in the world among all gifts.

sanskrit: annād balaṃ ca tejaś ca prāṇināṃ vardhate sadā annadānam atas tasmāc chreṣṭham āha prajāpatiḥ
english: From food the strength and the vital fire of living beings ever increase; therefore Prajāpati has declared the gift of food to be the best.

sanskrit: sāvitryā hy api kaunteya śrutaṃ te vacanaṃ śubham yataś caitad yathā caitad devasatre mahāmate
english: For from Sāvitrī herself, O son of Kuntī, you have heard the auspicious word, whence this is and how this is, at the sacrificial session of the gods, O greatly wise one.

sanskrit: anne datte nareṇeha prāṇā dattā bhavanty uta prāṇadānād dhi paramaṃ na dānam iha vidyate
english: When food is given by a man in this world, life-breaths too are given thereby; and than the gift of life-breath no higher gift is known here.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ hi te mahābāho lomaśasyāpi tad vacaḥ prāṇān dattvā kapotāya yat prāptaṃ śibinā purā
english: For you have heard, O mighty-armed one, that word of Lomaśa as well—what Śibi of old attained when he gave up his own life for the sake of a dove.

sanskrit: tāṃ gatiṃ labhate dattvā dvijasyānnaṃ viśāṃ pate gatiṃ viśiṣṭāṃ gacchanti prāṇadā iti naḥ śrutam
english: That same goal one wins by giving food to a brāhmaṇa, O lord of peoples; the givers of life-breath go to a most exalted goal—so have we heard.

sanskrit: annaṃ cāpi prabhavati pānīyāt kurusattama nīrajātena hi vinā na kiṃ cit saṃpravartate
english: And food itself arises from water, O best of the Kurus; for without that which is born of water, nothing whatsoever comes to be.

sanskrit: nīrajātaś ca bhagavān somo grahagaṇeśvaraḥ amṛtaṃ ca sudhā caiva svāhā caiva vaṣaṭ tathā
english: Water-born too is the blessed Soma, lord of the host of planets, and the nectar of immortality, and ambrosia, and Svāhā, and Vaṣaṭ as well.

sanskrit: annauṣadhyo mahārāja vīrudhaś ca jalodbhavāḥ yataḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ prāṇāḥ saṃbhavanti viśāṃ pate
english: Grains and healing herbs, O great king, and the creeping plants are sprung from water—whence the life-breaths of all that bear life come into being, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: devānām amṛtaṃ cānnaṃ nāgānāṃ ca sudhā tathā pitṝṇāṃ ca svadhā proktā paśūnāṃ cāpi vīrudhaḥ
english: The food of the gods is the nectar of immortality, and that of the nāgas is ambrosia; the food of the fathers is declared to be svadhā, and that of the beasts the creeping plants.

sanskrit: annam eva manuṣyāṇāṃ prāṇān āhur manīṣiṇaḥ tac ca sarvaṃ naravyāghra pānīyāt saṃpravartate
english: Food, the wise declare, is the very life-breath of human beings; and all of this, O tiger among men, arises from water.
